engine_label: DuckDB's PySpark API on this PC (not Apache Spark)
title: Notebook orchestration with runMultiple, parameters and exit values
objective_text: Run a parameterized notebook once per region, then a summary notebook after all of them, from one orchestrating notebook, and use the exit values the notebooks return.
scenario: Two notebooks already exist: load_region loads one region's orders and exits with how many rows it loaded, and build_summary totals the regions it's given. New regions appear without warning, so the orchestration can't list them by hand. Operations also wants a log of the rows each load reported.
starting_environment: Delta table bronze.orders, the notebooks load_region and build_summary in notebooks/, and a starter answer.py that loads one region.
required: gold.region_summary has one row per region in bronze.orders, with its order count and total amount.
ops.load_log has one row per region with rows_loaded, the integer that region's load_region run exited with.

expected.description: gold.region_summary: east 3 orders 30.25, west 2 orders 28.25. ops.load_log: east 3, west 2.

verifies: After your notebook runs, gold.region_summary and ops.load_log hold the right rows for every region, on the exercise data and on data with regions you haven't seen, on this PC.
rows_loaded is an integer, and running your notebook again leaves the same tables.
does_not_verify: It doesn't run on Apache Spark or in Fabric. Here runMultiple runs the notebooks one at a time, in an order that respects their dependencies; in Fabric they run concurrently on one Spark session, up to its concurrency limit.
Fabric's timeouts, retries and cross-workspace notebook references.
Running the notebooks from a pipeline's Notebook activity instead.

validation.fail: gold.region_summary isn't right: did every region load before the summary ran?

validation.pass: It also works when the regions change.
validation.fail: On other data the summary is wrong: work out the regions from bronze.orders.

validation.fail: ops.load_log doesn't match: use each load's exit value.

hints: Get the regions from the data: select the distinct region values from bronze.orders.
runMultiple takes a DAG: {"activities": [...]}. Each activity has a name, a path, args, and optionally dependencies, the names that must finish first.
The arguments' names must match the variables in the notebook's parameters cell exactly.
runMultiple returns a result per activity name; its exitVal is always a string.
explanation: notebookutils.notebook.run runs one notebook with arguments and returns the string it passed to notebookutils.notebook.exit. runMultiple runs a DAG of notebooks: independent loads can run together, and an activity with dependencies waits for the ones it names. Arguments replace the values in the notebook's parameters cell, so a misspelled name silently keeps the default. Deriving the regions from the data keeps the orchestration right when a region is added. Exit values are strings, so convert a count before storing it as a number.
troubleshooting: build_summary fails because a silver table doesn't exist: it ran before the loads. Give it dependencies.
A load wrote silver.orders_all: the argument's name doesn't match the parameter (region).
rows_loaded is text: convert the exit value with int().
reset: Reset rebuilds bronze.orders from setup.sql, removes the tables your runs made, and puts the starter back.
review_notes: Checked on Learn 2026-11-06 (notebookutils-notebook-run): run returns the string passed to exit, exit values are always strings, runMultiple takes a DAG with activities (name, path, args, dependencies) and runs notebooks concurrently with dependency relationships.
Sequential notebook.run calls in the right order also pass; the exercise grades the tables, not the API used.
